title: Add fastpath lint gate and compatibility shim for legacy build hooks
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: CI feedback for small changes has high latency because we run full lint/test matrices on every push. This PR introduces a lightweight fastpath lint lane that runs on path-aware changes and a compatibility shim that lets legacy node build scripts run inside a hermetic JS wrapper. The goal is to provide sub-2-minute lint feedback for the common small-change case while preserving full-matrix coverage on merge. Summary of changes: 1) New GitHub composite action .github/actions/fastpath-lint that performs file-list diff, computes a minimal lint profile from an incremental dependency graph cache, and dispatches either fast or full lint lanes. 2) New workflow .github/workflows/fastpath-lint.yml that triggers on PRs and PR_comment "run fast-lint" commands and prefers fastpath when changes are small and match allowlists. 3) Hermetic shim packages/ci-shims/legacy-build-shim that wraps legacy node scripts (old build hooks) in a minimal container-compatible runner so we avoid spawning host-level tooling on ephemeral runners. 4) Dep-graph cache: connect dependency-graph.json artifacts to actions cache to accelerate incremental analysis. 5) Minor package.json script changes and test harness tweaks to opt into the shim when CI_PRESENT=true. 6) Docs: CONTRIBUTING.md updated with the fastpath rules and how to opt out. Risks and mitigations: the path-aware heuristics can under-approximate impacted files for very large monolithic changes; to mitigate we default to full-matrix above threshold and added an explicit opt-out label ci/full-matrix. We also included a short roll-forward telemetry metric (ci.fastpath.hit_rate) so we can revert heuristics quickly if false negatives appear. Backwards compatibility: shim is additive and opt-in via environment variable so on-prem/private installs are unaffected until they adopt the shim. Testing and rollout plan: staged rollout via the staged-ci-lanes flag in the repo settings, initial opt-in for small teams for 2 weeks and experiment telemetery evaluated, then org-wide enable if stable. This PR bundles the tooling and a conservative policy; follow-ups will refine allowlists and expand the incremental dep-graph to TypeScript project references.
